## Benchmark Results: .NET 9 vs .NET 10

| Method | WordCount | .NET 9 Median (ns) | .NET 10 Median (ns) | Δ | Alloc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AverageWordLength | 100 | 1,604 | 1,640 | +2.2% | 0 B |
| WordLengthHistogram | 100 | 3,177 | 3,411 | +7.4% | 112 B |
| UniqueWordCount | 100 | 8,299 | 8,390 | +1.1% | 7,376 B |
| AverageWordLength | 1000 | 13,554 | 14,152 | +4.4% | 0 B |
| WordLengthHistogram | 1000 | 19,733 | 21,960 | +11.3% | 112 B |
| UniqueWordCount | 1000 | 84,418 | 90,100 | +6.7% | 73,152 B |

**Key takeaways:**
- **Memory allocations are identical** between .NET 9 and .NET 10 for all methods.
- **Performance is comparable**, with .NET 10 showing small regressions in the ~1-11% range. However, this machine is under load, so these differences are likely within noise — the IQR values are significant relative to the deltas.
- **No performance regressions of concern** for the upgrade. The differences are well within measurement noise on a loaded machine.

The benchmark project is at `TextAnalyzer.Benchmarks/` if you want to re-run on a quieter machine for more precise numbers.
